## Description

The `Chalk::Preprocessor::Heredoc` only transforms the first heredoc when multiple heredocs appear on the same line. The second (and subsequent) heredocs remain untransformed.

## Failing Test

`t/preprocessor/heredoc.t` - Test #11: "Multiple heredocs on same line"

## Steps to Reproduce

```perl
use Chalk::Preprocessor::Heredoc;

my $input = q{my ($a, $b) = (<<'EOF1', <<'EOF2');
First heredoc
EOF1
Second heredoc
EOF2
};

my $preprocessor = Chalk::Preprocessor::Heredoc->new(input => $input);
$preprocessor->transform();
my $output = $preprocessor->output;

print $output;
```

## Expected Output

```perl
my ($a, $b) = (q{First heredoc}, q{Second heredoc});
```

## Actual Output

```perl
my ($a, $b) = (q{First heredoc}, <<'EOF2');
Second heredoc
EOF2
```

## Analysis

The first heredoc (`<<'EOF1'`) is successfully transformed to `q{First heredoc}`, but the second heredoc (`<<'EOF2'`) remains in its original syntax.

This appears to be in the `find_heredocs_in_line` method at lib/Chalk/Preprocessor/Heredoc.pm:112, which should find all heredocs on a line but the transformation logic may not be handling multiple heredocs correctly.

- lib/Chalk/Preprocessor/Heredoc.pm:16 - `transform` method
- t/preprocessor/heredoc.t:200 - Failing test

## Impact

This prevents parsing of Perl code that uses multiple heredocs on the same line, which is valid Perl syntax commonly used in assignments and function calls.
EOF
